blackrock.reportedNotes:
- HireVue first: about 3 questions, roughly 2 minutes each with prep time
- Then several interviews, often framed around BlackRock’s principles, plus scenario questions
- Some roles add a task and a final round
- Why BlackRock (3)
- A recent global market or economic event and its impact (2)
- CV and past examples tied to BlackRock’s principles (1)
- Mostly behavioural, light technicals (2)

Sources: [Glassdoor, London analyst reviews 2024–26](https://www.glassdoor.ie/Interview/BlackRock-Interview-E9331-RVW91379954.htm) · [Glassdoor, further reviews](https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/BlackRock-Interview-E9331-RVW98487490.htm)

rothschild.reportedNotes:
- One-to-one first round (analyst + associate): CV, motivation, technicals
- Assessment centre with commercial awareness and market news
- Some offices run a group investment-case discussion
- Why Rothschild / what sets it apart from other banks (2)
- Valuation: DCF, methods and their assumptions (2)
- Equity bridge (enterprise value to equity value) (1)
- Market news and commercial awareness (1)
- Restructuring team is more technical than M&A (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, London analyst Apr 2025 + others](https://www.glassdoor.ie/Interview/Rothschild-and-Co-Interview-E9944-RVW96916386.htm) · [WallStreetOasis thread (older)](https://www.wallstreetoasis.com/forum/investment-banking/rothschild-first-round)

lazard.reportedNotes:
- London first round: about three behavioural questions, no technicals
- Other offices: technical phone screens (e.g. valuing a drug with a DCF)
- Why investment banking (1)
- DCF in a sector context (1)
- Interviewers push back on answers (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, summer analyst 2025–26](https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Lazard-Interview-E5784-RVW100668965.htm)

evercore.reportedNotes:
- London: CV screen, video interview, first round with HR plus technicals, assessment centre
- US rounds are heavily technical (incl. LBO-style cases)
- Accretion / dilution (1)
- Why Evercore and which industry (2)
- Hard technicals (3)

Sources: [Glassdoor, summer analyst 2025–26](https://www.glassdoor.com.au/Interview/Evercore-Interview-E2725411-RVW101217635.htm)

jpm.reportedNotes:
- London IB summer analyst: group activity, two fit interviews and one technical
- Elsewhere: HireVue (about 3 questions) then a superday of three interviews
- Walk through the three financial statements (2)
- Mix of fit and technical in each round (3)
- Commitment: would you accept an offer? (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, IB summer analyst 2026](https://www.glassdoor.ca/Interview/J-P-Morgan-Interview-E145-RVW102774299.htm)

gs.reportedNotes:
- HireVue (one report: 6 questions, 90 seconds each, mostly behavioural), then a superday of three interviews
- Reports are for Sales & Trading
- Know your CV in depth (2)
- Views on markets and the economy (2)
- Options / probability for markets roles (2)
- Mostly behavioural (2)

Sources: [Glassdoor, S&T summer analyst 2026](https://www.glassdoor.ca/Interview/Goldman-Sachs-Interview-E2800-RVW103673692.htm)

ms.reportedNotes:
- Online assessment, HireVue (3–5 questions), phone interview, assessment centre of three interviews
- Reports are for Sales & Trading
- Why Morgan Stanley / why this division (3)
- Current market news (2)
- Pitch a stock or a quick trade idea (1)
- Core values; a time you failed; handling pressure (2)
- Brain teasers (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, S&T summer analyst 2025–26](https://www.glassdoor.sg/Interview/Morgan-Stanley-Interview-E2282-RVW103595519.htm)

barclays.reportedNotes:
- London IB: case study, then three interviews (one goes through your case study)
- Why Barclays (over other banks) (1)
- Enterprise vs equity value (2)
- A deal you have followed (1)
- Mostly behavioural; easy-to-moderate technicals (2)

Sources: [Glassdoor, IB summer analyst 2026](https://www.glassdoor.sg/Interview/Barclays-Interview-E3456-RVW102790221.htm)

hsbc.reportedNotes:
- Online job simulation (situational judgement, written and timed video answers), HireVue interviews, then an assessment centre
- Values-based situational questions (2)
- Prioritising tasks / building a timetable on the spot (2)
- Recent events and why they interest you (1)
- Wealth-client case in a video interview (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, Global Markets summer intern](https://www.glassdoor.ie/Interview/HSBC-Interview-E3482-RVW71241352.htm) · [Glassdoor, summer analyst overview](https://static.glassdoor.es/Interview/HSBC-Summer-Analyst-Interview-Questions-EI_IE3482.0,4_KO5,19_IP2.htm)

citi.reportedNotes:
- London: online tests (Plum), first round of two interviews, assessment centre of three
- Introduce yourself; why banking and why Citi (1)
- Standard IB technicals (2)
- Case study with comps (some offices) (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, IB summer analyst 2025–26](https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Citi-Interview-E8843-RVW101158359.htm)

db.reportedNotes:
- London: three rounds (case study, technical, competency), about 45 minutes each, associate to MD
- DCF (1)
- Equity value to enterprise value bridge (1)
- Past experience and industry knowledge (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, IB summer analyst 2025–26](https://www.glassdoor.sg/Interview/Deutsche-Bank-Interview-E3150-RVW95052476.htm)

bofa.reportedNotes:
- London first round: about 25 minutes with an analyst, conversational
- Maths brain teasers (1)
- Behavioural questions (2)
- Financial statements and value bridges (US) (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, IB summer analyst](https://www.glassdoor.com.au/Interview/Bank-of-America-Investment-Banking-Summer-Analyst-Interview-Questions-EI_IE8874.0,15_KO16,49.htm)

ubs.reportedNotes:
- Online tests (numerical from charts, reading true/false), then HireVue: 5 questions, 30s to prepare, 2 min to answer
- Behavioural only at video stage (1)
- A time you worked outside your comfort zone (1)
- Where you see yourself in five years (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, graduate programme 2025–26](https://www.glassdoor.ca/Interview/UBS-Interview-E3419-RVW97951128.htm)

ey.reportedNotes:
- Online assessment: situational judgement, reasoning, numerical, recorded video answers
- A written email task analysing a profit and loss statement
- Assessment centre: group task, presentation, interview (often with a partner)
- Spot errors in financial data and explain them in a professional email (1)
- Link answers to EY’s values, especially integrity (1)
- Group problem-solving (2)

Sources: [Glassdoor, Audit graduate London 2026 + Edinburgh](https://static.glassdoor.de/Interview/EY-Audit-Graduate-Trainee-Interview-Questions-EI_IE2784.0,2_KO3,25.htm)

pwc.reportedNotes:
- Online assessment, recorded video interview (about 4 questions, 2 minutes each), virtual assessment centre, partner interview
- Behavioural and motivational questions (3)
- Detailed, specific examples (partner pushes) (1)
- Understand the role and PwC’s career path (1)
- Timed numerical questions (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, Audit graduate 2026](https://static.glassdoor.de/Interview/PwC-Interview-E8450-RVW103946350.htm)

deloitte.reportedNotes:
- London audit: presentation on set questions, then a motivational and strengths-based interview
- Some interviews go into the ACA qualification
- Strengths and motivation (2)
- Knowledge of the ACA qualification (1)
- Competency questions (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, Audit London 2024–26](https://www.glassdoor.com.au/Interview/Deloitte-Interview-E10177265-RVW92951198.htm)

kpmg.reportedNotes:
- Proctored online tests (situational, logical, numerical), recorded strengths-based video interview, assessment centre
- Assessment centre: group exercise (e.g. recommend a strategy for KPMG), then a partner interview
- Why KPMG and why this role (1)
- Time management (1)
- Group strategy exercise (1)

Sources: [Glassdoor, Graduate Audit UK 2025–26](https://www.glassdoor.ie/Interview/KPMG-Interview-E2867-RVW100390018.htm)
